paper_title: VisuoThink Empowering LVLM Reasoning with Multimodal Tree Search
caption: (LEFT) The trend of Pass@1 rate on Visual Navigation as the number of reasoning steps increases. (right) The relationship between the Accuracy@1 on geometry problems (Geomverse) and tree width for rollout search. We observe that LVLMs significantly benefit from longer reasoning chains, although the effect plateaus rapidly beyond a certain threshold of reasoning steps. The relationship between performance and tree width exhibits a more complex pattern, demonstrating an inverted U-shaped trend with both GPT-4o and Claude-3.5-Sonnet.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the relationship between Accuracy@1 (%) on geometry problems (Geomverse) and the number of child nodes (tree width) for two large vision-language models: GPT-4o and Claude-3.5-Sonnet. The x-axis, labeled "Num. of Child Nodes (Tree Width)", is linear and ranges from 1 to 7, with tick marks at each integer value. The y-axis, labeled "Accuracy@1 (%)", is also linear and spans from 15 to 35, with major gridlines at intervals of 5. The GPT-4o model is represented by a solid blue line with circular markers, while Claude-3.5-Sonnet is shown with a dashed light purple line and cross-shaped markers. For GPT-4o, accuracy increases from 24.4% at tree width 1 to a peak of 34.4% at tree width 5, then declines to 31.1% at tree width 7. For Claude-3.5-Sonnet, accuracy starts at 26.7% at tree width 1, rises slightly to 27.8% at tree width 3, then decreases to 24.4% at tree width 5 and further to 20.0% at tree width 7. Both models exhibit an inverted U-shaped trend, with performance peaking at a moderate tree width before declining.
